output.summary: KEP-1412 proposed an optional Immutable field on ConfigMap and Secret. When set to true, the apiserver rejects changes to data keys/values and to the Immutable field itself, and kubelets stop watching or polling those objects. The KEP reached stable status (implemented, stage stable).
output.rationale: The readme states the problem: any update to a Secret or ConfigMap propagates to all mounted Pods, so a bad push can break an application, and kubelets must watch or poll every referenced object, which costs apiserver load. Marking objects immutable protects against accidental outages and reduces control-plane load. The goal was reached through the code and documentation changes that the discussion records as complete before the status was set to implemented.

alternatives.option: Generalize immutability to all resource types (kubernetes/kubernetes#10179)
alternatives.why_not: wojtek-t said the particular semantic needed is not particularly useful for other resources, since the scalability goal requires that contents never change. He called the generalization complementary to this feature.

alternatives.option: Feature-gate the validation so that immutability is removed on rollback
alternatives.why_not: liggitt said he would not feature gate validation, because previously persisted data should still be honored. msau42 agreed that keeping the object immutable after rollback is the desired behavior.

evidence.quote: In this KEP, we are proposing to introduce an ability to specify that contents of a particular Secret/ConfigMap should be immutable for its whole lifetime.
If set to true, the machinery in apiserver will reject: - any updates explicitly changing keys and/or values stored in Secrets and/or ConfigMaps
the conclusion was that the particular semantic that we need isn't particularly useful for other resources.
I would not feature gate validation.
